title: Who the Sea Peoples were
summary: Egyptian records name groups who raided and invaded around 1200 BCE, but the origins of several, such as the Weshesh, are unknown. Many seem to have travelled by land.
why: They are bound up with the collapse of the Bronze Age world.

notes.problem: Open question had no theories (schema requires 2-4).

question: Who were the Sea Peoples who attacked Egypt, and where did they come from?
evidence: Recorded by Ramesses II, Merneptah (c. 1200 BCE) and Ramesses III at Medinet Habu (Year 8, c. 1175 BCE); 'Sea Peoples' is a modern label.
wouldSettle: Archaeological and genetic links between destruction layers, new settlers and named groups' homelands.

theories.name: Aegean origins
theories.idea: The Peleset (Philistines) are generally placed in the Aegean world; Ekwesh and Denyen are tentatively linked to Achaeans and Danaans.

theories.name: Western Mediterranean links
theories.idea: Some archaeologists tie the Sherden to Sardinia's Nuragic culture and the Shekelesh to Sicily, on sparse evidence.

theories.name: Anatolian homelands
theories.idea: The Lukka lands lay in later Lycia and Karkiya in western Anatolia; both groups appear in Hittite records.

theories.name: Refugees, not destroyers
theories.idea: Older work made them a cause of the Bronze Age collapse; recent work sees refugees fleeing a crisis already under way.
